cards.headline: US orders nonemergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia over Houthi attacks
cards.summary: The State Department ordered nonemergency government employees and their families out of Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks continue. The FT reports two people died in a drone attack on Aramco's Shaybah oilfield. Fox News says Trump is weighing direct strikes on the Houthis.
cards.why_it_matters: Americans in the kingdom face rising risk, and attacks on Saudi energy sites could push oil and fuel prices higher.

sources.title: US Orders Some Diplomats Out of Saudi Arabia Amid Houthi Attacks
US orders some personnel to leave Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks
US pulls personnel from Saudi Arabia as kingdom comes under Houthi fire

cards.headline: Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees in principle to resume talks
cards.summary: Missiles struck Kyiv after Russia said it is ready in principle to resume peace talks. Trump said the world is closest to ending the war, and tied his Russia sanctions waiver to the release of jailed American Stephen Hubbard.
cards.why_it_matters: The diplomacy involves US sanctions policy and a freed US citizen, while analysts say Putin feels little pressure to end the war.

sources.title: Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks
Trump links Russia sanctions waiver to release of jailed American
Rosenberg: US diplomatic push offers little hope for imminent Ukraine peace

cards.headline: Tesla profit falls 43% on flat revenue as Optimus production starts
cards.summary: Tesla reported $1.7 billion in net income on $28.0 billion in revenue, flat from a year ago, though results beat expectations. It began Optimus robot production in California while auto revenue declined.
cards.why_it_matters: Tesla's earnings and robot push shape a major US automaker's outlook, and merger talk with SpaceX adds uncertainty for shareholders.

sources.title: Tesla beats on earnings and sales even as auto revenue declines
Tesla starts Optimus robot production in California as profit falls 43%
Flying Roadsters can’t lift Tesla’s flat Q3 revenues

cards.headline: Meta to create non-voting share class to fund AI push
cards.summary: With its third-quarter results, Meta said it will issue a new class of non-voting stock, trading from 2027, to fund AI, acquisitions and pay. The FT reports it lets Zuckerberg sell stock without diluting control.
cards.why_it_matters: It shows how expensive the AI buildout has become, even for the richest tech companies, and what it means for investors.

sources.title: Meta to create a new class of shares to fund AI push
Meta agrees deal to keep Zuckerberg in California despite wealth tax proposal

cards.headline: IBM beats estimates as CEO touts AI traction
cards.summary: IBM beat Wall Street estimates on revenue and profit in its third quarter. CEO Arvind Krishna said the company is helping clients adopt artificial intelligence.
cards.why_it_matters: IBM is a read on whether corporate customers are paying for AI, a key question for tech stocks.

sources.title: IBM beats on top and bottom lines as CEO Krishna touts 'Super Intelligence' traction

cards.headline: White House gives Politico 48 hours to retract stories
cards.summary: The White House counsel's office told Politico in a Monday letter it has 48 hours to retract or correct stories about alleged staff drama or face unspecified consequences, Axios reports. The deadline expires Thursday.
cards.why_it_matters: The demand raises questions about the relationship between the government and the press.

sources.title: White House to Politico: Retract stories or face "consequences"

cards.headline: Democratic groups sue over Trump election prosecution threats
cards.summary: Democratic groups sued the administration, arguing it uses unfounded voter fraud claims to pressure states and election officials. Top Democrats on the intelligence committees say they expect Trump to allege foreign meddling. The administration has cited concerns over noncitizen voting.
cards.why_it_matters: The dispute over federal and state roles in running elections arrives two weeks before Election Day.

sources.title: Democrats accuse Trump of using prosecution threats to pressure election officials
Top 2 Democrats on Intel say they're preparing for Trump to claim foreign meddling
House Republicans subpoena New Jersey secretary of state over noncitizen voter registration

cards.headline: Trump rallies in South Carolina as GOP eyes Mississippi, Kansas
cards.summary: Trump headed to South Carolina to back Sen. Darline Graham, who is favored but faces a strong challenge from Democrat Annie Andrews. Axios reports Senate Republicans are weighing more money for South Carolina, Kansas and Mississippi.
cards.why_it_matters: Races once seen as safe are tightening, widening the fight for Senate control.

sources.title: Trump heads to South Carolina to boost Senator Darline Graham in race
Scoop: Senate Republicans fear Mississippi is in play
Cook Political Report polls find Democrats leading three critical Senate races

cards.headline: Poll shows record support for Democrats; GOP holds spending edge
cards.summary: An NPR poll found record support for Democratic congressional candidates, with voters wanting Congress to check Trump. The FT reports Republicans and affiliated groups hold a large spending advantage, per filings.
cards.why_it_matters: Money and polling point in different directions with two weeks left before the midterms.

sources.title: Poll: Voters want Congress to be a check on Trump, trust Democrats more on issues
Republicans head into midterms with huge spending advantage

cards.headline: AIPAC ends endorsements and direct PAC contributions
cards.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee's PAC is reportedly no longer endorsing candidates or making direct contributions after three cycles, saying endorsements, direct contributions and earmarking will not be part of its approach, in favor of what it calls new tools.
cards.why_it_matters: It changes how a major pro-Israel lobby influences US campaigns during the Iran war.

sources.title: AIPAC ends endorsements and PAC contributions in favor of ‘new tools’

cards.headline: Administration asks Supreme Court to allow Big Bend wall work
cards.summary: Solicitor General D. John Sauer filed an emergency petition asking justices to lift a lower court injunction halting border wall construction in Texas's Big Bend region, calling the block baseless.
cards.why_it_matters: The ruling will affect border policy and how courts can restrain federal construction projects.

sources.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to allow Big Bend border wall construction
Trump administration asks Supreme Court to lift block on Big Bend border wall construction

cards.headline: Judge rejects EPA bid to dismiss data center pollution suit
cards.summary: A court ruled the EPA cannot unilaterally dismiss a pollution lawsuit over a SpaceXAI data center, rejecting the administration's claim, Ars Technica reports.
cards.why_it_matters: It bears on how much power federal agencies have over environmental suits as data centers draw voter scrutiny.

sources.title: Judge rejects Trump’s wild claim EPA can dismiss data center pollution lawsuits

cards.headline: Iran says it will keep uranium as odds of renewed war rise
cards.summary: Tehran said it had nothing new to tell Washington after mediators reportedly offered new nuclear proposals, and is determined to keep its uranium, Al Jazeera reports, amid a flurry of diplomatic meetings.
cards.why_it_matters: The nuclear dispute is central to whether US-Iran fighting resumes, with consequences for oil prices.

sources.title: Iran determined to keep uranium amid increased war odds, flurry of meetings

cards.headline: Persian Gulf oil flows near pre-war levels, but prices may stay high
cards.summary: October oil exports from the Persian Gulf nearly returned to levels seen before the Iran war, MarketWatch reports, though traders remain wary of a fragile recovery and prices may not fall soon.
cards.why_it_matters: Gasoline and diesel prices depend on whether Gulf supply holds.

sources.title: Oil is now flowing out of the Persian Gulf like before the Iran war. Why prices may still not come down anytime soon.

cards.headline: Mexico charges ex-prosecutor with treason over US-joined drug raid
cards.summary: Mexican authorities charged former prosecutor Cesar Jauregui Moreno with treason, accusing him of allowing US agents to join an April raid on a suspected drug lab. Questions remain over whether Mexican law was followed.
cards.why_it_matters: It exposes friction over US agents operating in Mexico as the two countries cooperate on drug enforcement.

sources.title: Ex-prosecutor charged with treason in Mexico over US drug raid
Mexico charges prosecutor with treason over US involvement in drug raid

cards.headline: Colombia seizes 7.6 tonnes of cocaine in decade's biggest haul
cards.summary: Colombian authorities seized 7.6 tonnes of cocaine at the Caribbean port of Cartagena, the largest haul in a decade, Al Jazeera reports.
cards.why_it_matters: Cocaine supply from Colombia feeds US drug markets and shapes Washington's relationship with Bogota.

sources.title: Colombia seizes 7.6 tonnes of cocaine in biggest haul in a decade

cards.headline: Cuba says US is threatening countries before UN embargo vote
cards.summary: Havana accused Washington of threatening countries with retaliation if they refuse to vote against condemning the US embargo at the UN. The US position was not given in the report.
cards.why_it_matters: The vote tests US diplomatic standing on Cuba policy.

sources.title: Cuba accuses US of threatening countries ahead of UN embargo vote

cards.headline: Bolsonaro adviser says Petrobras would get freedom without privatization
cards.summary: An energy adviser to Flavio Bolsonaro told Bloomberg that if he wins Brazil's Oct. 25 runoff, Petrobras would get broad freedom to reshape its portfolio and attract private investment, with no privatization.
cards.why_it_matters: Brazil is a major oil producer, and the runoff outcome could influence energy markets and investment.

sources.title: Bolsonaro to Unleash Petrobras Without Privatizing, Adviser Says

cards.headline: Pope needs no further treatment after lung cancer surgery
cards.summary: Test results confirmed the pope's diagnosis as a localised lung adenocarcinoma, and he does not need further treatment after surgery, the BBC reports.
cards.why_it_matters: The health of the head of the Catholic Church is closely watched by more than a billion followers worldwide.

sources.title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery

cards.headline: Nigeria's first Ebola patient holidayed in Uganda, officials say
cards.summary: Officials say the wife of a diplomat based in Abuja, Nigeria's first confirmed Ebola case, traveled to Kampala for a vacation, adding to regional spread questions.
cards.why_it_matters: Cross-border travel links in the outbreak complicate containment efforts.

sources.title: Nigeria's first Ebola patient holidayed in Uganda, officials say

cards.headline: Moderna to release Phase 3 data on cancer vaccine this weekend
cards.summary: Moderna will reveal full Phase 3 trial results for its custom cancer vaccine this weekend. MarketWatch says the stock is among the year's strongest because of the treatment and a lot rides on the data.
cards.why_it_matters: Personalized cancer vaccines could change treatment if the trial results hold up.

sources.title: Moderna is about to release the trial results for its cancer vaccine. A lot is riding on this data.

cards.headline: EQT agrees €9.6 billion deal for Qiagen
cards.summary: Private equity firm EQT agreed to acquire molecular testing company Qiagen for about €9.6 billion ($10.8 billion), ending years of takeover speculation, Bloomberg reports.
cards.why_it_matters: The deal shows private equity appetite for diagnostics companies that supply US labs and hospitals.

sources.title: EQT Reaches €9.6 Billion Deal for Molecular Testing Firm Qiagen

cards.headline: Flapping Airplanes raises $1 billion at $6 billion valuation
cards.summary: A year-old AI lab, Flapping Airplanes, raised a $1 billion Series A nine months after a $180 million seed round. Legal AI startup Legora separately raised $550 million at an $8.8 billion valuation.
cards.why_it_matters: Venture money keeps flowing to AI startups even as credit markets question AI infrastructure debt.

sources.title: Year-old AI lab Flapping Airplanes raises $1B at a $6B valuation
Legal AI startup Legora raises $550M Series E at $8.8B valuation

cards.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Duet agent; Meta's Muse passes 10 million users
cards.summary: Anthropic released Claude Duet, an AI agent for professionals and small businesses, as a research preview. Meta said its Muse AI app has over 10 million users, with shopping a top activity.
cards.why_it_matters: AI agents that act on users' behalf are becoming mainstream consumer products.

sources.title: Anthropic takes on Muse with Claude Duet, its new AI agent
Meta says Muse has over 10M users, with shopping a top activity

cards.headline: Walmart to let AI agents shop on its site for customers
cards.summary: Walmart will let customers use an AI agent on its website next month, with approval, review and spending limit controls. Amazon, by contrast, blocks AI agents from shopping on its site.
cards.why_it_matters: Retailers are choosing opposite approaches to automated shopping, which could change how Americans buy.

sources.title: Walmart is inviting AI agents to shop for you
While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat

cards.headline: Recursive releases Flint, a laptop coding model built largely by AI
cards.summary: Startup Recursive released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model it says was built largely by its own AI research system, as an early test of AI that improves itself.
cards.why_it_matters: Self-improving AI is a central safety and competitiveness question for the industry.

sources.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI
This Startup Is All In on Recursive Self-Improvement. Its Latest Model Is Scary Good

cards.headline: GM plans fully self-driving private cars by 2028
cards.summary: GM's product chief Sterling Anderson told the FT the automaker plans fully self-driving private vehicles by 2028. A new central computer debuts in the 2028 Cadillac Escalade IQ, and OnStar gets an AI overhaul.
cards.why_it_matters: It shows Detroit trying to match Tesla and Chinese rivals on autonomy and software.

sources.title: GM aims to leapfrog rivals with new generation of autonomous cars
GM is betting compute and AI will help it compete with Chinese automakers

cards.headline: Air Force says it needs 1,509 combat-coded fighters by 2035
cards.summary: A new Air Force report calls for 1,509 combat-coded fighters by 2035, with F-35s about 40% of the fleet and F-47s replacing F-22s. An official said a new-build F-16 is under consideration but not urgent.
cards.why_it_matters: The plan frames how much Congress may be asked to spend on air power.

sources.title: Air Force needs 1,509 combat-ready jets by 2035, service tells Congress
US Air Force outlines the fighter fleet it needs by 2035

cards.headline: New Mexico sues Epstein's attorney and accountant
cards.summary: New Mexico's attorney general filed a civil lawsuit against Jeffrey Epstein's longtime attorney Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn, alleging they facilitated and concealed his crimes in exchange for generous salaries.
cards.why_it_matters: The suit targets Epstein's financial and legal enablers, not just Epstein himself.

sources.title: Epstein’s attorney and accountant accused of ‘facilitating and concealing’ his crimes in lawsuit

cards.headline: Thousands of California state workers strike for a day
cards.summary: Thousands of California state employees, including nurses and teachers represented by SEIU Local 1000, began a one-day strike seeking higher wages, telework and affordable healthcare after a contract lapse.
cards.why_it_matters: The walkout affects state services and tests labor relations in the nation's largest state workforce.

sources.title: Thousands of California public employees begin strike over contract

cards.headline: Toledo chemical tank explosion forces mass evacuation
cards.summary: A tank explosion in Toledo, Ohio, released an airborne irritant that can burn the eyes, nose, mouth and skin, prompting a mass evacuation. One first responder was injured, officials said.
cards.why_it_matters: Residents near the site face health risks while the cause is investigated.

sources.title: Chemical tank explosion in Toledo, Ohio, prompts mass evacuation

cards.headline: Taiwan charges five men over plot to run down comedian
cards.summary: Taiwanese prosecutors charged five men over a plot to ram a car into comedian Huang Yi-hao, who mocks Xi Jinping. They say a person from China identified as K paid the defendants.
cards.why_it_matters: Taiwan has repeatedly accused China of transnational repression, a growing flashpoint in cross-strait tension.

sources.title: Taiwan charges five men over plot to run over comedian for his Xi Jinping jokes

cards.headline: Tunisia jails US-Tunisian opposition politician for four years
cards.summary: Olfa Hamdi, a US-Tunisian national, was convicted of plotting and inciting the military to disobey orders over social media posts and sentenced to four years in prison.
cards.why_it_matters: A US citizen is jailed over speech, raising concerns about political repression in Tunisia.

sources.title: Tunisia jails opposition politician for four years over social media posts

cards.headline: Indonesia faces its worst wildfire season in a decade
cards.summary: Indonesia is dealing with its worst wildfire season in a decade, with peat fires burning in central Kalimantan, the BBC reports.
cards.why_it_matters: Peat fires release large amounts of carbon and haze that can harm health across the region.

sources.title: Why is a peat fire so bad? BBC is in Indonesia to find out

cards.headline: Airbnb bans hosts from requiring guest chores
cards.summary: Airbnb's updated house rules policy, for reservations booked on or after Nov. 20, bars hosts from asking guests to do time-consuming chores such as dishes or trash. Some hosts are threatening to strike.
cards.why_it_matters: It changes what travelers can be asked to do on one of the largest US rental platforms.

sources.title: Airbnb bans making guests do dishes and take out the trash
Airbnb Hosts Are Furious They Can No Longer Make Guests Do Their Chores
